clue.text: Be unable to stand trial after sighting of Parisian

indicators.note: the trial comes after the French word has been seen, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: de is the French word for 'of', as a Parisian would say it
a test is a trial or examination

explanation.surface: Someone cannot face a court case after spotting a Frenchman in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be unable to stand' looks like failing to face trial, but it is the definition: to loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to be unable to bear it, the idiomatic sense of 'can't stand'.

clue.text: Swapped ends when using ragged garden tool

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word for ragged change places

parts.note: ragged means teased, ribbed

explanation.surface: A gardener swaps the ends of a worn tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swapped ends' exchanges the first and last letters of RIBBED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dibber is a pointed hand tool used to make holes in soil for seeds or bulbs.

clue.text: Crossed lines occurring in traditional housing

indicators.note: housing means the word for traditional holds the lines

parts.note: trad is short for traditional, as in trad jazz
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Crossed phone lines happen in old-fashioned houses.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to go across, so crossed and traversed are synonyms.

clue.text: Second question about folio one poses

parts.note: how is a question word
of can mean about, as in 'speak of'

explanation.surface: A second question is raised concerning a folio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one poses' reads like asking a question; it is someone who poses to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a person who flaunts themselves, an exhibitionist.

clue.text: Fox almost seizes turkey, one of a certain age

indicators.note: seizes means the shortened word for fox wraps round what follows
almost means the last letter of the word for fox is dropped

parts.note: to fox someone is to trick or fool them
a turkey is a fool, as is an ass
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fox nearly catches a turkey on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizes' puts ASS plus I inside TRIC, the word for fox missing its last letter. 'of a certain age' points to a geological period.
explanation.definitionFit: Triassic describes the geological period opening the Mesozoic era, so it means belonging to one particular age.

clue.text: Stream learners attending religious class

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, a school subject
L is learner, as on a learner driver's plate, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Learner groups are streamed into a religious studies class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stream' looks like a school ability group; it is a brook. L plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small brook or rivulet.

clue.text: Gypsy returned to harbour pub, having a jar

indicators.note: to harbour is to hold within, so the reversed word wraps the pub
returned says the word for Gypsy is read backwards

parts.note: Roma is the name of the Romani people
PH is public house, as on maps

explanation.surface: A traveller heads back to the harbour pub for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives AMOR. 'jar' looks like a pint at the pub; it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient jar used for wine or oil.

clue.text: Maintaining beat in midsection, busker hummed

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the middle letters hold the word for beat
in midsection picks the middle two letters of busker

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A street musician keeps the rhythm and hums along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hummed' looks musical beside 'busker'; it means smelt bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hummed is British slang for smelt unpleasant, the same as reeked.

clue.text: Study news written in revolutionary language

indicators.note: written in places the study and news letters inside the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
to eye is to study, look at
N is new, so news is two of them

explanation.surface: Studying news written in a revolutionary's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as the plural of new, giving N twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheyenne is the Algonquian language of the Cheyenne people of the American plains.

clue.text: Type of school's right-wing recruitment slogan?

definitions.meaning: ... schools were high-performing English schools picked to share good practice with others
split 2-1-3 the letters urge people to become a Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A school's motto that sounds like a call to sign up to a right-wing party.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, CON is short for Conservative, so a slogan inviting recruits might say 'BE A CON'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beacon status was given to top-performing English schools under a government scheme, making it a category of school.

clue.text: Potter makes this error — green spilled over, and blue ultimately

parts.note: a slip is a small error

indicators.note: spilled over says the word for green is tipped over, read backwards

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of blue

explanation.surface: A potter's blunders: green glaze slopping over, finishing in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled over' reverses RAW to WAR. 'Potter' looks like Harry Potter, but it is a ceramicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipware is pottery decorated with slip, a liquid clay, so it is something a ceramicist produces.

clue.text: Celebrity and girl briefly turned up where heavenly bodies are seen

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: turned up says the short girl's name reads upwards, reversed in this down answer
briefly says the girl's name is cut short to its first few letters

parts.note: Pamela is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a girl appear somewhere glamorous people are spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly bodies' looks like gorgeous celebrities; it means stars and planets.
explanation.definitionFit: A star map is a chart of the night sky showing where stars and constellations appear.

clue.text: Gnasher's still at centre of tomfoolery in the comic

indicators.note: in means the word for still and the middle of tomfoolery go inside the rearranged word
comic marks the letters of the word 'the' as rearranged for laughs

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'yet to come'

indicators.note: centre of picks the two middle letters of tomfoolery

explanation.surface: A comic strip character's teeth stay at the heart of the clowning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges THE as ETH. Gnasher is the dog in the Beano comic, but here it is slang for a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnasher is slang for a tooth, and the eye tooth is the canine below the eye.

clue.text: Data PC stores about police regularly receives approval

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: receives means those letters take in the word for approval
regularly picks alternate letters of police, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: OK is approval

explanation.surface: A police computer holds information and gets a nod of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes O, I, E from 'police'; OK goes in after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookie is a small data file a website leaves on a computer to remember the user.

clue.text: Bottomless spirit and French wine belonging to a medieval house

indicators.note: bottomless removes the last letter, the bottom in a down answer

parts.note: an angel is a spirit
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Endless spirits and French wine at a medieval banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angevins were the Plantagenet kings descended from the counts of Anjou.
explanation.definitionFit: Angevin describes the house of Anjou, the Plantagenet dynasty that ruled England from 1154.

clue.text: Appeal forces landowner to regenerate part of Essex

parts.note: SA is sex appeal
F is the physics symbol for force, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: to regenerate is to remake, so the letters of landowner are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A public appeal pushes a landowner to redevelop a stretch of Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to regenerate' rearranges LANDOWNER into RONWALDEN. Saffron Walden is a market town in Essex, a county north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron Walden is an Essex market town, so it is a portion of that county.

clue.text: Person to whom work and play are the same

definitions.text: Person to whom work and play are the same

parts.words: Person to whom work and play are the same
parts.note: a playwright's job is writing plays, so a play is literally a piece of work

explanation.surface: Someone who loves their job so much it never feels like labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright's works are plays, so for this writer work and play are one.

clue.text: Norwegian, American, German and Japanese currency

parts.note: und is German for and
the sen is a Japanese coin, a hundredth of a yen

explanation.surface: A list of nationalities and a foreign coin, like a joke's setup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word; with 'German' it gives UND.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen was the Norwegian explorer who first reached the South Pole.

clue.text: Around summer, fifty per cent failed medical aid class overseas

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the half of summer
failed shows the letters of medical aid have collapsed into a new order
fifty per cent takes half of summer, its last three letters

explanation.surface: Over the summer, half the medical aid failed to reach people abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges MEDICAL AID, which goes 'Around' MER, the second half of 'summer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle America is the conservative American middle class, a social group across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Couple rejected stuffing in case that's supremely flashy

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so the reversed couple goes inside

parts.note: lest means in case

indicators.note: rejected says the couple is turned back, read upwards

parts.note: a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: A couple turn down a stuffed suitcase as far too flashy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DUO to OUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud means garish, so the superlative is the most garish of all.

clue.text: Mirror writer's extremely immature, penning useless articles

parts.note: the writer refers to themselves, I am, contracted

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the outer letters hold the junk
extremely takes the outer letters of immature

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless stuff

explanation.surface: A writer's mirror is childish, crammed with junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' means the setter's 'I'm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror someone is to copy them exactly.

clue.text: Sweary vagrant in chippy?

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters of the word stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A foul-mouthed tramp turns up in a fish and chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippy' looks like a chip shop or a touchy mood; it is a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British slang for a carpenter, and one who saws timber is close kin, hence the query.

clue.text: Working for retirement, mum gets Happy Meal

indicators.note: for retirement says the word for working goes back, reversed

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
mum means hush, keep quiet, SH
up means happy, in high spirits

explanation.surface: A worker retiring is treated by their mother to a fast-food kids' meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' reverses ON to NO. 'Happy Meal' looks like the fast-food name, but Happy and Meal do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosh-up is British slang for a big, hearty meal.

clue.text: Crouch, heading in third, smothered by most of team

indicators.note: smothered by puts the letter beneath the team in this down answer
most of drops the last letter of the team word

parts.note: a squad is a team

indicators.note: heading in picks the first letter of third

explanation.surface: A crouching player, third in line, buried beneath a team pile-on.
explanation.definitionFit: To squat is to crouch down on one's heels.

clue.text: Repeatedly note currents swirling in lake

indicators.note: repeatedly says the note is given twice

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: swirling turns the pair of currents round, reading them backwards

parts.note: AC is alternating current, here twice for the plural

explanation.surface: Musical notes and swirling currents in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' reverses the pair of currents to give CACA; AC is alternating current.
explanation.definitionFit: Titicaca is the large lake on the border of Peru and Bolivia.

clue.text: Part of face one should start jeering? Hooter

indicators.note: start picks the first letter of jeering

parts.note: an owl hoots, so it is a hooter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' looks like slang for a nose, near 'Part of face'; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A jowl is the lower jaw or the fleshy part of the cheek beneath it.

clue.text: Impudent person putting slug on dressing

indicators.note: on puts the word for slug after the dressing in this across answer

parts.note: a sauce is a dressing for food

clue.text: Reason why broadcast is shown on hospital computers etc

indicators.note: is shown on puts the sounded letter after the hospital and computers in the across answer

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
IT is information technology

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken, giving a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word why is said aloud

explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' gives Y; 'is shown on' puts it last. 'Reason' looks like a cause; it is a sound mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind, the ability to think clearly, is sanity.

clue.text: It's a pleasure no former volunteer exaggerated

parts.note: the TA was the Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve, now renamed the Army Reserve
a tall story is an exaggerated one

explanation.surface: An ex-volunteer insists that serving was no pleasure after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) was Britain's volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are polite replies to thanks, meaning the help was no trouble.

clue.text: Kitchen assistant perhaps glazes terrine partly

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next
